tested:
Bare "iosv-*" image folder format (no "cisco-" prefix) - some real IOSv uploads use
this naming instead of "cisco-iosv-*". Found missing 2026-07-22 (the project owner: "How hard can
it be to categorise those IOL images properly?") chasing a live failure: image
"iosv-159-3-m6" had NO profile match at all (get_profile_key returned None), so it fell
through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE's 120s boot_timeout_sec and got none of the extended
busy-console retry treatment node_config._retry_deadline_s gives any profiled device -
it was still running the original fixed-2-attempt budget the whole night. Same specs as
"cisco-iosv" above (identical underlying software, just a different upload naming
convention) - see that entry's comment for the 400s boot_timeout_sec evidence.

reasons.day0_channel: NPX-4299 (rule #59, the project owner 30 Oct 2026): FAT config DISK as hdb holding ios_config.txt (GNS3 way, CVAC); EVE-NG has no boot-time vIOS config - see providers/day0_iso_channels.py FatConfigDiskChannel.
reasons.emulator:
cpu_model host + qemu_arch x86_64 (NPX-1527 GW-AUTH/PROFILES-TOOLS pass-3, rule #59):
same fix as "vios"/"viosl2" (NPX-460) for the identical documented live crash
(memory-pool corruption -> CPU exception vector 4) - this key is what
PROFILES["cisco-iosv"] is actually aliased to below, so this is the value real
imports of either naming convention boot with.
